Commentary.Commentary: The target is not a big one and with the wicket still a good one to bat on, Pakistan are expected to chase this down. Will they do so or do New Zealand have some fight left in them? We won't know that today but we surely will get some idea about which way the game is heading. 10 exciting overs left in the day. Join us in a while to catch the action.

New Zealand went into their second innings with a trail of 74, they got off to the worst starts possible as they lost Latham early. Kane and Raval did try and steady the ship but a few quick wickets saw the visitors reeling at 108 for 4. However, a magnificent partnership between Nicholls and Watling brought the tourists back into the game. Pakistan though came out all guns blazing after the Tea break and now are favorites to win this game.

From 220 for 4, New Zealand have been bowled out for 249. They had no answers to Yasir Shah and he finished with a fifer. Hasan Ali started things off for Pakistan and he was the one who ended it. He too bagged a fifer to his name. The two shared 10-wickets amongst them.

What a session this has been till now for Pakistan, they have ran through the lower-order in no time and now the advantage is with them as they only have to chase down 176. Nicholls and Watling were cruising, the two added a 112-run stand with both crossing their half centuries. They were batting with no problem whatsoever but then Yasir Shah came to life. He got Nicholls first and that brought about the downfall.

Yes! He can! Five-fer for Hasan Ali! His first ever in Test cricket. Pakistan have wrapped up things in style. Hasan bangs it short on off, Boult looks to pulls this but is very late in doing so. He then checks his shot and the ball takes a top edge and balloons towards short covers. Hafeez won't take a simpler catch ever. Five wickets for Yasir and Hasan. Who gets the ball? New Zealand all out for 249 and set Pakistan a target of 176.
Almost gets it! Hasan Ali bowls it on a length around off, it pitches and comes back in. Boult tries to defend but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Trent Boult is the last man in.

OUT! Knocked over! No. 9 is down now. A length delivery around off, it comes back sharply. Sodhi maybe expecting a short is one is rooted to the crease. He tries to keep it out but misses and the ball clips the bails. 4-fer for Hasan Ali. He has 4 balls to take a 5-fer.
Works it with the angle towards mid on for a run.
Outside off and beaten again, the batsman fails to put bat on ball.
Almost bowled, Sodhi goes for the defense but the ball turns sharply and beats the bat as well as the off stump. Great bowling by Yasir!
Darted in on off stump, Sodhi tries to defend but gets a thick edge that runs to point.
Wide outside off, Sodhi plays the square drive towards point.
Around the wicket to the leftie, Ajaz goes for the huge one. The ball goes in the air and the gap as well. Deep square leg comes around to stop the ball as the batsmen run only one.
Fuller and outside off, Sodhi drives to sweeper cover for a single.
Beaten comprehensively outside off! The ball was full and moves away after landing. Ajaz plays completely down the wrong line to this.
Good ball on top of the off pole, Ajaz defends it but gets the inside edge onto the pad and the ball rolls onto the ground on the leg side.
Fuller and drifting onto the pads, Sodhi tucks it behind square leg for a single.
Same ball again but this time Ajaz connects it and gets it in the gap and runs it down to third man for three runs. All valuable runs.
Shorter in length this time, Ajaz is fishing for it outside off and is lucky not to get an edge.
Around the wicket and beats the outside edge! On a good length and shaping away after landing, Ajaz wants to defend but misses it.
Hasan Ali is back on.
On the shorter side and outside off, Sodhi looks to cut but gets a bottom edge towards point.
BEATEN! This is nicely tossed up around off, drawing the batsman onto the front foot. Sodhi leans and tries to drive but the ball whizzes past the outside edge.
FOUR! Up and over! These are handy runs for New Zealand. Sodhi brings out the slog sweep again, hits it over the mid-wicket region and into the fence.
A big swing to a tossed up ball outside off, Patel swings goes for the slog sweep but it goes off the inner half through mid-wicket for a run.
The googly on middle, Patel keeps it out.
This is timed through covers for a run.
This one bounces a bit more than normal and misses the bat as Ajaz looks to defend. It hits the pad high on the knee roll so there was not much of an appeal.
Drawn ahead by the flight on this one, but Patel manages to defend it with full face of the bat being shown.
Shorter and quicker on middle, the batsman has defended it by covering the spin on this one.
Falls just wide of short leg! This one is again full and outside off, turns in a long way to take the inside edge and the ball drops away from short leg luckily for Ajaz.
This one is a carbon copy of the previous ball, and Ajaz does well to defend it off the middle of the bat.
Full and outside off, Ajaz has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Flatter on middle, punched back to the bowler.
This is really full, almost yorker length. Sodhi just manages to keep it out.
Shorter and outside off, it is played to the point region by the batsman.
Some finesse after the slog. Sodhi gets outside the line of the ball and paddles it fine on the leg side for a couple.
SIX! Overpitched and on middle, Sodhi gets under it and lofts it over deep mid-wicket for a huge one. Every run is important here. Beautiful connection on this one though.
Flatter and outside off, Sodhi tries to cut but misses the ball.
Floated ball outside off, driven to covers. 228/8.
Arm ball on off, tucked around the corner. Dot ball.
Gives this air on the pads of Sodhi. He turns it away getting an inside edge to the on side. They cross.
Short and over the stumps, can't get it past the point region.
Tossed up ball around off, once again hit back to the bowler.
Full and down leg, played with a straight bat back to the bowler.
Ajaz Patel is the new man in.

OUT! TIMBER! What a peach! They're falling like nine pins now! Beautifully tossed up outside off and Yasir has given this ball revs. It pitches and then turns in a long way. Wagner tries to defend with a lunge but with a gaping hole between bat and pad. The ball goes through after spinning a crazy amount and hits the off pole. Fifer for Yasir Shah, his 14th in Test cricket! He has completely turned the game on its head.
This ball is on middle and holds its line and bounces a bit more as Wagner defends off the back foot.
This one is on middle and leg and straightens a bit after landing. Wagner keeps it out.
Full and outside off, Wagner is half ahead in defense.
Drinks Break! Meanwhile Neil Wagner joins Sodhi out in the middle.

OUT! Another one bites the dust! All it needed was a wicket and now Pakistan are electric. 1, 2 and now 3 wickets for Yasir in three overs. This was dragged down a bit. Watling rocks back to pull it but gets but the ball stays a touch low. Goes under the bat and hits him on the thigh pad. The players put in an appeal and the umpire raises his finger. Both the set batsmen are now back in the hut. Pakistan would now look to run through the lower order.
Loopy ball around off, Watling taps it to the on side.
Shorter and on off stump, Sodhi remains in his crease as he defends it.
Full face of the bat as Sodhi defends it back to the bowler.
Full and on off now, Sodhi comes ahead and defends it.
Down the leg side again, Sodhi plays it fine on the leg side. The ball is stopped just inside the boundary and the batsmen pick up two.
Sprayed way down the leg side. Sarfraz does well to bring his pads together and stop any byes.
Fuller and on middle, Watling goes down and sweeps it fine on the leg side for a single.
Haris Sohail back on now.
Things are really happening now ! This one lands on middle and rips away at the last moment to beat the outside edge of Sodhi who is front in defense.

OUT! Grandhomme has reviewed here, he has been given LBW and Hawk Eye returns three reds. A waste of a review by Grandhomme. That was absolutely plumb. He bags another failure and New Zealand have now lost two in quick succession. This one is pitched on middle and turns to hold its line. Grandhomme is on the back foot and wants to flick it away to the leg side but misses and the ball hits him bang in front of middle on the back pad. The players appeal and the umpire raises his finger. Grandhomme reviews but to no avail. The visitors now have lost both their reviews and are also losing their way now.
Goes for the sweep shot but misses.
On the middle pole, it is flicked to mid-wicket.
It was at this period of time yesterday that the light started to get a bit dim. Let's hope we get a full day of proper cricket.
Colin de Grandhomme now needs to be more watchful. Has to stick around with his partner and see out as much as the day possible.
Another inside edge! This time it was full and on middle, Watling comes ahead to defend and there is too little turn on this one. The ball gets the inside edge and rolls to the left of short leg.

That was a close shave! The ball is flat and outside off, Grandhomme looks to drive it on the back foot, but gets the inside edge that misses the leg stump by a whisker and runs down to fine leg for a run. The lead is now 150!
In the corridor of uncertainty, it is blocked.
Back of a length around off, Watling gets right behind the line and defends it onto the ground.
On the off pole, the batsman is solid in defense.
Good length outside off, Watling makes a leave.

A little away movement there after it pitches on middle, de Grandhomme tries to put bat on ball but gets a leading edge towards mid off. The fielder there has a shy at the non-striker's end but misses.
This is on the pads, it is worked through square leg for a run.
Wider outside off on a short length, Grandhomme punches it to cover off the back foot.
Flatter ball on off, Grandhomme shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the backfoot.
Colin de Grandhomme is the new man in.

OUT! Yasir strikes! A huge breakthrough for Pakistan! Nicholls has been sweeping well all innings but this one is a tad too full outside off to play the shot. It kisses the under edge and Sarfraz takes a wonderful catch. He goes up in an appeal immediately and the umpire raises his finger. Henry however, reviews after a chat with his partner. Replays show that there is an under edge. Nicholls has been given his marching orders. Pakistan get one of the two well-set batsman and this should pump them up, their shoulders were starting to drop. End of the 112-run stand and the visitors now have half the side back in the hut. They are effectively 146 for 5.
Big moment in the game! Nicholls has been given out caught behind. He though has reviewed.
Full and outside off, Nicholls smothers it by coming well ahead.
Drifting onto the pads with a flatter one, Watling tucks it around the corner on the leg side for a single.
Shorter and on off stump, Watling goes on the back foot and plays it to mid on.
Dug in short. Nicholls is ready for it and pulls it away to deep square leg for 2 runs.
A tad fuller this time, Nicholls drives to mid off who dives and stops the ball.
Similar delivery and similarly defended again.
Outside off on a length again, HN plays it into the ground.
Sprayed down the off side, Nicholls just leaves it alone.
Good length and on off stump, Nicholls defends with ease.
Full and on the pads again, poor bowling. Watling flicks it straight to short mid-wicket though.
On leg stump again, Watling guides it to short mid-wicket.
Shortens the length and turns it into the pads, Nicholls plays it toward deep square leg for a run.
Around the wicket to the leftie, pitches it wide outside off. Nicholls comes ahead and defends.
Short and flat outside off,  cut away behind point for three runs.
On the pads to start off with, Watling works it towards square leg for a couple.
Yasir Shah is into the attack now.
Length ball outside off, cut away to point. Maiden over.
Bowls this full on that fourth stump channel in search of swing. Nicholls drives it to covers.
Down leg, Nicholls hops a tad and tucks it to the on side.
Good length ball away from the off pole. Henry leaves it alone. No swing here and the new ball hasn't done much.
On the money is Abbas. Henry is happy to defend it.
On a good length down leg, Nicholls tucks it away.
This is on good length, Watling comes half forward and defends it easily.
Short and on off stump, Watling stands tall and defends it.

FOUR! Beautiful timing on this occasion towards the mid-wicket fence. It brings up BJ Watling's 15th fifty in Tests. It has been a wonderful innings with a lot of application. The Kiwi wicket-keeper has a knack of playing these grinding innings in pressure situations and here he is again with one more. Coming to the delivery, it was full and on the pads. Easy pickings for someone who's been at the crease for this long. Flicks it away. This also brings up the 100-run stand between these two. What a partnership it has been, taking the game slowly away from Pakistan's grip.
Good length and on the pads, Watling flicks it towards mid-wicket for a couple.
Full and at the pads, Nicholls  has flicked the ball off his pads towards fine leg. One run added to the total.

Good length outside off, Watling tries to guide it between third slip and gully. They run through for a quick one and Babar Azam has a shy at the striker's end. Hasan Ali backs up the wayward throw in time and prevents overthrows.
Similar length and holds its line after pitching, Nicholls is well ahead and punches it to mid off.
A tad wider this time, Nicholls leaves it alone as it moves away after landing.
Around the wicket, good length and just outside off. Nicholls defends it to mid-wicket.
Length ball on top of off, Nicholls defends it straight back to the bowler.
Close! This one is full and on middle, Nicholls looks to play it toward mid on but gets the leading edge that runs along the ground to backward point.
Good length ball just outside off, Nicholls defends it coming half ahead.
Good length ball on middle, slightly moving away after landing. Watling adjusts well to the swing and plays it down towards point.
This one moves away after landing, Watling doesn't go chasing after it though.
Outside off and on a good length, Watling lets it go through to the keeper.
Another bouncer but the ball didn't rise as much as the previous one. BJ ducks under it.
Short again but on top of off stump, Watling remains on his back foot to defend.
This one is short and outside off, Watling defends it off the back foot.
Wide! Too high. Bouncer and aimed at the helmet, Watling ducks and lets it go. The leg umpire signals it as Wide.
Pitched slightly ahead on this occasion, Nicholls comes ahead and defends.
Short of a good length and just outside off, Nicholls defends it from within the crease.
Down the leg side and short, Nicholls wants to flick it away but the ball was too far away and thus, lets it go.
This one is on middle and worked down to square leg but no run.

Huge appeal from Pakistan! Was it the outside edge or the thigh pad? The ball was a really good one and Nicholls was completely squared up by this one. Good length just outside off and the batsman was ahead to defend it but the ball just shapes away very slightly. There is a noise as the ball passes the bat. Ultra Edge shows that the noise was of the bat hitting the pad as it comes down.
Good ball on a length outside off, Nicholls leaves it watchfully.
Way outside off stump again, Watling wants nothing to do with it.
This one is well outside off, the ball is left alone by Watling.
Good length outside off, rock solid in defense again.
Fuller this time, Watling wants to drive it through the covers but gets the inside half of the bat and the ball runs down to mid on.
Good length well outside off, slightly shaping in, left alone.
No ball! Overstepping by Hasan Ali! Quite a big one at that. The ball was short and outside off, defended on the back foot.
Good length on off stump, Watling comes ahead to defend it.
Hasan Ali to bowl from the other end.
Just short of a good length on top of off stump, Nicholls punches it off the back foot to mid on.
Outside off on a length, Nicholls lets it go through.
Over the wicket now. Starts off on leg stick, Nicholls defends back to the bowler off the back foot.

Abbas pulls up! He comes running in from over the wicket but then sees the batsman standing in the wrong position so bails out. The umpire then asks the batsman to change ends and we are all set to go now.
The second new ball has been taken now. Will it provide Pakistan the breakthrough they are looking for?
Length ball outside off, Nicholls is half forward in defense.
Slightly fuller and angling in on middle, tucked away behind square leg for a run by Watling.
Good length and a tad outside off, Watling shoulders his arms to it.

The players are back on the field for the final session of play. 33 overs to be bowled in the remainder of the day. BJ Watling to face the first ball after the break. Mohammad Abbas to start off the proceedings. Here we go...
... Day 3, Session 3 ...

New Zealand's session and comprehensively so! There has not been a single wicket to fall in this session and even chances were far and few. Watling and Nicholls have blunted the threat of the spinners and have looked very comfortable out there in the middle. The unbeaten 92-run stand couldn't have come at a better time but there is so much time left in the Test and the pitch seems to have really eased out, so it is imperative for them to continue. Will they or will Pakistan break the stand with the new ball which is available now? Join us in a bit for the last session!
Changes the angle for the last ball! He floats it up middle, it is blocked well. TEA ON DAY 3!
Very full on middle, Nicholls jams it out to short leg.
Gives it a nice loop around off, it spins in. Nicholls tries to defend but the ball goes off the inner half towards short leg.
Floats it up on off, it is blocked.
Down the leg side, it is flicked towards deep square leg for a run. 200 up and the lead is now 126.
This is tossed up on off, Watling strokes it to mid off.
Bowled short and on off stump, Nicholls rocks back and attempts to cut it away. He just manages to get the under edge and the ball rolls down to the fielder at point.
Flatter and quicker on middle, Nicholls prods ahead to dead bat this one.
Shorter this time outside off, punched away straight to extra cover. Azhar Ali stumbles and falls down while fielding it. It doesn't cost a run though.
Well outside off on a length and turning away, left alone.
Flighted and the ball is almost on yorker length, Nicholls digs it out.
Well looped up delivery on middle, Nicholls brings his bat in front of the pad and defends.
This is on the stumps. Blocked.
Goes back and then punches it through covers for a run.
Quicker and on off, it is defended.
This is tossed up outside off, Nicholls tries to drive but gets it off the inner half towards the bowler.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
This is down the leg side, the batter works it to short fine leg.
Length ball on middle to which Watling comes down the wicket and plays it to mid on. No run taken though.
Similar ball slightly wider this time, Watling prods forward and defends it into the ground.
Fuller and on off, kept out by Watling coming ahead.

Fifty up for Nicholls! The ball is on the pads and is worked behind square on the leg side. They pick up a single and it brings up the 6th Test 50 for Nicholls. This is a really important innings in the context of the game. The key has been his patience. He walked in when his team was in a lot of trouble and has batted very sensibly to reach here. Must carry on though.
Shorter in length this time, Nicholls defends off the back foot.

Immediately paid off! Leading edge and just goes above Hafeez's head. The ball was on length and turned away after landing. Nicholls closed the face of the bat too soon and gets the leading edge but his luck is good today and survives. The ball runs to the left of mid off and the batsmen come back for two.
Mohammad Hafeez is now on.
Clever bowling! It is the slider after the last ball which turned. Watling though plays for the original trajectory and keeps it out.
BEATEN! This is flighted on off, it pitches on off and then turns square. The batter lunges to keep it out but is beaten by the spin.
Loopy ball on leg stump, the batsman plays it onto the ground.
This is given nice amount of air, the batsman strokes it towards mid on for a quick run.
This is given air on middle, it is flicked to short mid-wicket.
On the shorter side, it is worked with the turn towards mid-wicket.
Down leg, worked through square leg for one.
Goes the other way. Outside off, picked up by Watling and creams it to extra cover. They manage to come to come back for the third.
Off spinner on off, Watling bunts it down.
A bit shot outside off, punched off the back foot through covers. Another run taken.
Loopy ball around off, Nicholls blocks it out.
Arm ball comes into Watling. H rocks back and looks to cut it but gets a bottom edge towards short third man. One run taken.
On middle, it is defended.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman.
Drives it with the turn to mid on.
Flighted ball on off, Nicholls blocks it out.

Just wide! A half-chance that! This was tossed up outside off, it comes back in. Nicholls defends inside the line, the ball goes off the inner half, uppishly towards short leg. Imam there dives full stretch to his right but can't reach to it.

NOT OUT! And Pakistan now have lost both their reviews. A massive inside edge there. This was tossed up outside off, it turns in a little. Nicholls lunges to defend but the ball hits his pads. An appeal follows but the umpire shakes his head. After a chat Sarfraz signals the 'T'. They go upstairs and replays show that there is bat involved.
Review time! A huge appeal for an LBW has been turned down. Pakistan have reviewed. Impact looks outside off, Nicholls is the man in question.
On the stumps, it is defended.
Down the leg side, left alone.
Flighted ball on middle, the batsman works it to mid-wicket.
This is flatter and on middle, it is worked around the corner for a single.
Flatter and on middle, Nicholls pushes it to covers.
Worked with the turn towards backward square leg for a run.
Bilal Asif is back on.
Gives this a nice loop, the ball pitches and bounces a touch extra. Nicholls tries to defend but the ball hits him high on the bat. Luckily though is goes onto the ground.
The batsman has punched that ball through the offside. They pick up a single.
The flipper on off, the batsman punches it to covers.
On the shorter side, it is punched to covers.
Flighted on middle, Watling defends it off the front foot.
On middle, it is blocked.
Flighted ball on off, Nicholls lunges and keeps it out.
Floats it up on off, it is kept out.
On the shorter side, Nicholls goes down on one knee and pulls it through square leg for a couple.
Bowls this one flatter and on off, the batsman rocks back and keeps it out.
Gives it air around off, Nicholls is solid in defense.
Very full outside off, Nicholls mistimes it through covers. Abbas gives it a chase and the batsmen run two.
Floats it up on off, the batsman lunges and blocks it out.
Plays the sweep again towards short fine leg. A run taken this time.
Plays the sweep but it goes off the inner half towards short fine leg.
Gives it a nice loop outside off, Nicholls reaches out for it and then blocks it out.
Another tossed up ball outside off, HN lunges and defends it.
The leg spinner around middle, Nicholls with the turn works it to square leg.
Yasir Shah is back on.
SHOT! But just one. Short ball down the leg side. Henry pulls it with disdain. Imam at short leg gets a piece of it. It goes to deep square leg and the batsmen cross.
Loopy ball on off, Henry leans forward and blocks it out.
HN has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Outside off, cut in the gap through cover-point for an easy run.
Full and down leg, Watling flicks it to the on side.
Flatter ball over the stumps, Watling punches it to covers.
Outside off, punched off the back foot towards covers.
Back of a length ball way down leg, Nicholls leaves it alone. A good take from Sarfraz.
FOUR! Hasan digs in a bouncer down leg. Nicholls well in control of it pulls it fine through fine leg. No protection there and a boundary results.
Drags his length back a bit from the previous ball, outside off. Henry drives it to the off side.
Full and on off, Nicholls blocks it out with a straight bat.
Yorker. Full and on the off pole. Nicholls does well to jam it out.
This one is flatter in trajectory, Watling keeps it out.
Full and slightly outside off, it is defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
This one is short and on middle, Watling punches is straight back.
This is full and well outside off but Henry takes a large stride ahead and sweeps it behind square on the leg side for a run. This also takes the lead to 100.

Appeal for LBW, but there was an inside edge on that one. This ball is outside off and turns in quite a bit after landing. Nicholls fails to cover the turn completely and is lucky to get the inside edge.
Full to start off with outside off stump, Nicholls comes ahead and dead bats it.
Haris Sohail is into the attack now.
Fuller and outside off, Watling drives it straight to the cover fielder.
Well outside off on a length, Watling leaves it alone.
Good pace from Hasan Ali here! This one is fuller and on middle. Watling plays it to mid on with a straight bat.
On a good length and on middle stump this time, Watling plays it back to the bowler.
FOUR! Overpitched and Watling is onto it immediately. Angling onto middle and leg, the Kiwi batsman flicks it to the right of short mid-wicket and times it beautifully.
Slightly short of a good length, Watling defends it off the back foot to cover.

Shorter again and turning into Nicholls' pads. He flicks it away towards square leg and runs the first one quickly, putting pressure on the fielder who misfields it, allowing them to come back for a comfortable couple in the end. The lead has swelled upto 95 now.
This one turns a lot after landing, Nicholls looks to work it away behind square leg but misses it to get hit on the pad. But the ball is turning too much so there is no appeal.
This one is shorter and wide outside off, Watling cuts it away to the fielder deep on the off side for another single.
Good ball this time! Just outside off, Watling comes ahead and defends it well though.
Around the wicket this time, flatter and turning into the pads, Nicholls rocks back and works it away towards square leg for another run.
Flatter and outside off, Watling cuts it away towards sweeper cover for a single.
Around the wicket to the left-hander, Nicholls defends it coming half-forward to this one which is on good length and outside off.
Just as I say he is bowling tight lines, he darts one in at the hips. It is worked away by Watling behind square leg for a single.
Hasan is pegging away at the off stump, short of a length this time. Watling defends it comfortably.
Similar length but slightly closer to the off pole this time due to which Watling decides to defend it with his willow.
This one is left alone by BJ as the ball is on length and well outside off.
Length ball outside off, Watling punches it to point off the back foot.
Hasan Ali is back on.

FOUR! Reverse swept and it has been hit well! This is full and outside off, Nicholls gets to the pitch of the ball as he takes a huge stride and reverse sweeps to the third man fence all along the ground.
This one rares up off a good length and turns to beat the inside edge of Nicholls who comes ahead to defend. The ball was rising as it hits the pads, hence there is not much of an appeal.
Fuller and flighted again outside off, Nicholls sweeps it away to square leg. No run though.
Shorter and turning into the pads, Nicholls flicks it onto the leg side but straight to the fielder.

Around the wicket to the leftie, just falls short of short leg! The ball was outside off, lands on a rough patch and turns in quite a lot to take the inside edge of Nicholls' bat who was trying to defend on the front foot.
Good flighted ball outside off, Watling gives his partner the strike by driving it to sweeper cover.
Nicholls is looking solid here as keeps another full one out comfortably.
Fuller and on middle, The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

The ball is drifting onto the pads on this occasion, Nicholls flicks it through mid-wicket for a couple. It brings up the 50-run stand between these two. Good stand this! Needs to continue though. The lead is now 84.
Well flighted outside off and turning away, Nicholls doesn't find the need to play at it.
Looped up on off, Nicholls takes account of the spin and defends it well.
Length delivery and turning away outside off, Nicholls cuts it away in the gap through point for a couple.
Slightly fuller on middle, driven down the ground by Watling but there's no run available.
Well outside off, left alone.
Faint outside edge but it was soft hands so that ball just drops down in front of slip. It was looped up on off stump and turned away slightly at the last moment.
No run.
Similar ball but this time he sweeps it squarer this time and picks up a run.
Nicholls is taking large strides to make sure he takes LBW out of question. He sweeps this full one from outside off to short fine leg.
This one is short and on off stump, Nicholls punches it through the covers for a single and keeps the strike.
Fuller and outside off, The batsman drives this through the covers but no run.
This one is darted in quicker and shorter on middle. Nicholls gets behind the line of the ball and defends.
FOUR! 150 up for New Zealand! Welcome boundary for them, one must say! The ball is flighted and overpitched outside off, Nicholls sweeps it away to the square leg fence.
Fuller and well outside off on this occasion, Nicholls keeps it out.
Good ball! This one is well bowled on off stump and turns slightly. But the ball is well dealt with by Nicholls.
Shorter ball on off stump, the batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the backfoot. Maiden over.
Flatter delivery at a quick pace. Watling comes forward to defend it again.
Looped up this time outside off, driven to mid off by Watling.
Fuller and quicker outside off, driven straight to cover.
Fuller and on off stump, Watling smothers the spin on this one by defending it into the ground.
Flatter and outside off, Watling punches it straight at silly point on the bounce. He's not hurt though.
Changes the angle for the left-hander and bowls it from over the wicket. It is outside off and it has been left alone.

In the air... but safe! The bounce there surprised Watling. This is slightly shorter around off, it pitches and then takes off. Watling was shaping up for playing the pull shot but then seeing the bounce, checks his shot. It goes uppishly towards square leg for a run.
Gives it air on off, the batsman defends it off the front foot.
Shorter and outside off, Nicholls goes back and punches it towards cover for a run.
This is driven crisply towards the cover fielder who makes a good stop to his right.
This is worked through square leg with the turn for a run.
Fuller and outside off, Nicholls comes ahead to defend and is struck on the pad but impact is outside off so there is no problem here for the Kiwi.
Nicholls takes a large stride and sweeps it to short fine leg. No run though.
This one is way outside off, Nicholls prods ahead and pads it away. The ball lobs onto the leg side. No risk involed here.
Flighted well outside off, Nicholls is drawn forward and his attempted forward defense takes the inside edge. Luckily for him, it drops away from the short leg fielder.
Flat again and outside off, Watling cuts it away to point again and picks up a single. Extra bounce on this one.
Flatter and well outside off, Watling cuts it straight to point.
Yasir Shah is back into the attack now.

A short delivery to end the over, Nicholls pushes it back towards mid on. Bilal is getting turn but it is slow turn, also the ball which have turned are pitched outside off, so nothing for the batsman to worry about.
Another loopy ball on off, Henry blocks it onto the ground.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Gives it nice amount of air on off, HN prods forward and keeps it out.
Flatter and on off, Nicholls goes back and defends it onto the ground.
Nicely tossed up around off, the batsman lunges and keeps it out.
This ball is on the pads and is played by Henry with the angle towards square leg for a run.
This ball is on a good length and on middle, Nicholls plays it to mid on with a straight bat. No run.
This is well outside off on a length, Nicholls shoulders arms to it.
The ball is just short of a length and Nicholls goes back and defends with a straight bat.
Slightly fuller than a good length, the batsman flicks it away to deep square leg for a single.
The keeper has come up to the stumps. The ball was on good length and outside off, defended by Watling to short cover.
Short and on middle, Nicholls stays in the crease and defends.
This ball is flatter and turning into Watling, he rocks back and pulls it to deep square leg for a run.
Flatter ball on off, Watling covers the turn and defends it.

Huge appeal from Pakistan but the umpire is not fazed. The ball was flighted on off stump and spinning in slightly, Watling goes down and attempts to sweep this one but misses it to get hit on the pads. After a long discussion, Sarfraz decides not to go for the review. The replays show that the ball hits his forearm before going on to hit the pads. So that's a good decision by Pakistan not to go upstairs.
Looped on off stump, Watling plays it with soft hands onto the ground on the leg side.
Flighted in on middle, Watling comes ahead and defends it on to the leg side.
Full and angling in on middle again, Watling flicks it again but this time short mid-wicket dives to his right and keeps it down to a single.
FOUR! Wonderful flick off the pads and this time in the gap. The ball is overpitched and at the pads, easily worked square on the leg side to the fence.
Full and on the pads, Watling flicks it off his pads straight to short mid-wicket again.
On middle this time, Watling works it to mid-wicket.
Just outside off, Watling is half forward to this one and defends it to cover.
Good length ball on the off stump, Watling defends on the front foot.
Spins and beats the edge! Nicholls comes forward to defend the ball outside off on a full length and the ball turns away to beat his outside edge.
This one is well outside off, left alone by the left-hander this time.
Slightly flatter this time outside off, Nicholls goes on the back foot and plays it to short cover.
Even more loop this time, Nicholls keeps it out again.
Looped up outside off again, Nicholls covers the spin and defends.
Flighted just outside off, Nicholls prods ahead and defends.
Bilal Asif to bowl from the other end.
Good comeback from Abbas. Apart from the first ball the rest were on point. This one is on a good length, BJ punches it back ahead.
On a good length around off, Watling plays it to the of side.
Full again on off, bunted down.
A tad fuller around off, Watling keeps it out.
That is the Abbas we know. Length ball in line of the stumps, Watling blocks it out with a straight bat.
Comes in from over the wicket and lands it short and wide. A rare loosener from Abbas. Cut away past point for a brace.
We are back for the afternoon session. BJ Watling and Henry Nicholls will continue their innings. For the hosts, Mohammad Abbas will bowl the first over.
... Day 3, Session 2 ...

New Zealand will be disappointed as there were not many questions that the pitch was throwing at them. They needed a bit more application. Having said that, take nothing away from the Pakistan bowlers. They toiled hard and got their rewards. They will look to come back and do more of the same. Join us for the post Lunch session in a while!

Pakistan's session without a doubt! 3 massive wickets and almost another one towards the end of the session. The first one being the biggest, the New Zealand skipper. Ross Taylor entertained till he was there in the middle but played one shot too many and got caught plumb in front by a Hasan Ali special. The latter picked up one more as he had the well-set Raval caught behind.
Outside off, left alone. THAT WILL BE LUNCH ON DAY 3!
BYE! Down the leg side, Watling goes for the pull but misses. The keeper fails to collect it cleanly. The ball rolls towards short fine leg and a bye is taken.
This is tossed up on off, blocked.

NOT OUT! Missing leg! Did not see that coming to be honest. Excellent use of the technology though by New Zealand. This is tossed up around off, it turns back in after pitching. Watling shuffles across and goes on the back foot, he tries to flick but misses to get hit on the pads. An appeal follows and the umpire agrees. Watling walks upto his partner and then signals the 'T'. Replays roll in and it shows it is going down leg. Watling survives to fight another day and New Zealand there will breathe a sigh of relief.
Watling is a goner! He has been given out LBW but he has reviewed. Looks out to be honest.
Works it with the turn to mid-wicket.
Gives it air around off, the batsman keeps it out.
Well bowled and also well played! This is pitched on off and then straightens. It also bounces a touch. Nicholls first tries to defend but then seeing the extra bounce, pulls his bat out of the way.
Attacks the off pole again, HN blocks it onto the ground.
Around off, the batsman gets right behind the line and defends it.
On the pads, it is worked to fine leg for a single.
On the fuller side and it comes in a touch. The batsman strokes it towards silly mid on.
Length again and outside off, the batsman shoulders arms to it.
On off, blocked.
Well bowled! This is flatter and around off, it pitches and straightens a touch. HN goes back and plays inside the line to get beaten.
Uses his feet and then works it through mid-wicket to rotate strike. A good partnership building here for New Zealand.
The off spinner on middle, Watling works it to short leg.
Shorter and outside off, Nicholls goes back and slaps it through point for a run.
Slightly shorter and on off, the batsman flicks it through mid-wicket for a couple.

Again a straighter line. It seems to be a plan with two mid-wickets in place, they are hoping for the batsman to flick it uppishly to one of the two. That does not happen though as Watling flicks it all along the ground to the man at mid-wicket.
On the stumps and it is flicked to mid-wicket.
A little too straight this time, BJ works it to mid-wicket.
On the fuller side and it tails back in a touch. The batsman strokes it back to the bowler.
Length again and around off, it is kept out.
Good length on off, the batsman defends it onto the ground.

Top edge but safe! This is flighted outside off, Nicholls tries to sweep but the extra bounce causes problems. It takes a top edge but lands in no man's land at the short fine leg region. Couple taken. Sarfraz was heard telling be ready for the top edge but not sure to which fielder. The top edge was induced but there was no fielder there.
Gives it a nice loop on middle, HN prods forward and tries to keep it out.

Good turn there! However, it needed to bowled a little more closer to the off pole. This is floated outside off, Nicholls first thinks of playing at it but then seeing the turn, pulls out of the shot.
On the shorter side, the batsman goes onto the back foot and pulls it towards deep square leg for a run.
Goes down on one knee and paddles it fine down the leg side for a run.
Gives it air on off, Watling lunges and blocks it out.
Bilal Asif is into the attack.
Full and around off, Nicholls reaches out to it and strokes it to covers.
On off and it is kept out. This is the line he bowls on regular basis, however, he has been a little too wide outside off today.
Comes around the wicket but the line is not the right one, it is outside off and the batsman lets it be.
Closer to the off pole this time, Nicholls gets right behind the line and defends it.
Good length again and outside off, the batsman once again does not fiddle with it.
On a length and outside off, the ball is left alone.
Mohammad Abbas is back on.
This is quicker and a bit shorter on middle, Watling goes back and whips it through mid-wicket for a brace.
Gives it a nice loop and the batsman keeps it out.
Down the leg side, Nicholls waits for the ball to do its bit and then works it fine down the leg side. Three taken.
The is flighted outside off, it is kept out.
Brings out the sweep shot but misses and is hit on the pads. No risk what so ever as Nicholls plants his front foot out of the line of the off stump.
Tosses it up around off, Nicholls lunges and defends it out.
On the shorter side, the batsman defends it onto the ground.
On the shorter side, Nicholls swivels and pulls it through square leg for a run.
On the fuller side, the batsman drives it square on the off side but finds the fielder.
Good length and around off, it is blocked.
Loose, loose stroke! Short and wide outside off, Nicholls goes to cut away from his body but luckily for him he gets beaten.
Back of a length on off, it is kept out.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Flatter and on off, the batsman keeps it out.
FOUR! Picked the line of the delivery quickly there. This is down the leg side, Watling quickly goes down on one knee and paddles it fine down the leg side. It races away to the fence.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Gives it air on middle, it turns away ever so slightly. Watling tries to flick but gets a soft leading edge towards covers.
This is floated around off, the batsman sweeps it through square leg for a run.
On the shorter side, Watling stands tall and defends it onto the ground.
Another inswinger from off, BJ is solid in defense.
Full and wide outside off, it comes back in but not enough to make the batsman play.
On a length and around off, it is kept out.
Better! Bowls it closer to the off pole, it is kept out.
FOUR! A freebie for Watling to get off the mark! Short and wide outside off, BJ cuts it through backward point for a boundary.
Gives it a little more air this time and Nicholls it solid in defense.
On the shorter side, Nicholls defends it onto the ground. Yasir should probably bowl from the over the wicket angle, threatening both the edges, just might create more opportunities.
Down the leg side, the batsman misses the flick.
Brings out the sweep but mistimes it through square leg.
Another leg spinner and Nicholls works it around the corner for no runs.
Gives it air outside off, Nicholls works it to mid-wicket with the turn.
On a length and around off, Watling keeps it out. Brilliant over by Hasan, three runs and two wickets from it.
BJ Watling is the new man in.

OUT! EDGED AND TAKEN! Second in the over and New Zealand are now in big, big trouble. Raval falls four shot of a fifty. Excellent stuff by Hasan Ali. He got the right hander with the in-dipper and now gets the left-hander with an awayswinger. On a length and around off, it is first angled into the batsman and then gets it to shape away a touch late. Raval plays inside the line, the ball kisses the outside edge and Sarfraz Ahmed behind makes no mistake. Pakistan are ecstatic at the moment and New Zealand are effectively 34 for 4.
Good aggression by the bowler! Full and on off, it is driven back to the bowler. He mimes a throw at the striker's end and then gives the batsman the stare. He has his tail up at the moment.
Goes for the yorker but ends up bowling a full toss, the batsman strokes it through mid on and collects three. Nicholls is off the mark with that.
Back of a length on off, Nicholls defends it onto the ground.
Henry Nicholls is the new man in.

OUT! That is absolutely plumb in front! Hasan Ali strikes! Probably the first ball which has come in a long way and it has provided the wicket for Pakistan. On a length and around off, it comes back in late. Taylor plants his front foot right across and then fails to adjust to the in-dipper. He misses the flick and the ball hits the front pad. An appeal follows and the umpire raises his finger straightaway. Taylor starts walking back as he knew he is a dead duck.
Works it against the turn for a single through mid-wicket. Taylor has scored all the runs in this partnership which is worth 19 at the moment.
Quicker again and it is in that in-between length. Taylor is not sure whether to play it off the front or the back foot. He in the end defends it from within his crease.
Flatter and around off, Taylor defends it onto the ground.
Taylor dances down the track but does not get to the pitch of the ball. He defends it.

Has that been dropped? Well, judging by the reaction of the Pakistan players, it does seem so. Would have been a freakish dismissal. Taylor has absolutely creamed that towards silly point who takes evasive action. The ball hits his boot and lobs up towards Yasir who dives forward and tries to take it but fails to do so. Would not have mattered though as the ball bounced before hitting the foot.
Gives it a nice loop around off, it turns away. Taylor makes a leave.

Drinks break! A very good hour of play for the New Zealanders if you take out the wicket of their skipper. They have wiped off the deficit and the pitch looks pretty easy to bat on now. Williamson will be kicking himself for a lapse of concentration. Pakistan will be happy and look to pick another wicket or two before lunch.
Another bumper to end the over! Raval ducks under it with ease.
A little too wide outside off, left alone.
Another short ball but with not a lot of fizz. Raval gets behind the line and defends it onto the ground.
A good change in length there! A well-directed bouncer by Ali. Raval ducks under it at the very end.
Length again around off, Raval gets forward and blocks it out.
Good length and just outside off, Raval makes a leave.
Shorter and quicker this time on middle and leg, Taylor steps back and defends it with a straight bat. Good ball to end the over which had 14 coming off it.

FOUR! This is the third boundary in the over. Taylor steps down the wicket and lifts it over mid-wicket this time. The ball is quick and on middle. Taylor comes down and converts it into a half-volley as he continues to be aggressive and counter-attacking against the leg spinner.
Short and well outside off again, Taylor cuts again but this is straight to the point fielder.
FOUR! Short and outside off again, Taylor cuts it again, this time to the right of point and for four again. The hundred is up for the Black Caps. The Pakistanis are feeding Taylor with bad balls.
FOUR! This is a poor ball outside off, Taylor cuts it behind point for four. Backward point dives but can't stop this one. Taylor is playing a lot of shots this morning.
Flighted outside off, Taylor comes down the wicket and drives through the covers for a couple.
On the middle stump this time, Raval is solid in defense.
On a good length and angling away from the left-hander, Raval lets this one go.
Short of a good length and on middle, Taylor plays it down the ground with a straight bat and goes to the other end.
On a good length and middle this time, Taylor stays back and defends to mid on.
This is slightly fuller and on off, driven hard but straight to mid off.
Good length ball just outside off, Taylor comes ahead and defends it with the full face of the bat.
Full and quick on middle again, Taylor sweeps it again but middles it this time. Goes straight to backward square leg for a run.
The ball is fuller and on middle now, Taylor goes for the sweep. The ball takes the top edge and goes in the air toward fine leg for a couple.
Ross Taylor walks out to the middle.

OUT! Bowled 'em! A peach out of nowhere from Yasir Shah. The New Zealand skipper has a lapse of concentration and plays back to a ball that he should've probably been ahead to. The ball is around middle and turns away very slightly. Enough to beat the outside edge of Williamson's bat as he is looking to defend. The ball seems to have clipped the off pole and the Pakistan players start celebrating. The umpire though, just to be sure, take it upstairs to check if the stumps have not been disturbed by Sarfraz. Replays roll in and it shows Yasir has cleaned Williamson up. Huge wicket in the context of the game! The stand of 86-runs comes to an end and Williamson walks back after getting a start. New Zealand in a spot of bother, they are effectively 12 for 2.
Shorter and spinning into the pads this time, Raval plays it to deep square leg for a run.
Pitched wide outside off, Raval takes a big stride forward and defends it into the ground.
Around the wicket to the left-hander now. An extra man around the bat now at silly point. The ball is flighted outside off, Raval comes ahead to defend it.
Good length ball on middle, Williamson is half ahead as he plays it mid on.
Short of a length and outside off. Kane ducks down and lets it go through.
Good ball this time, slightly quicker and keeps a little low. Williamson gets down and keeps it out well.
Drifting onto the pads this time, Williamson plays it to short mid-wicket. No run.
Outside off on a length this time, Williamson plays a good looking shot to cover.
On a good length, outside off. Williamson cover the line of the delivery and defends it.
The ball is not doing a lot for the Pakistan and the two batters are playing quite comfortably.
Hasan Ali is now into the attack.
Outside off, driven away to sweeper cover for a single.
Looped on off, Kane prods ahead and smothers the spin on this one by defending it into the ground.
Quicker at the pads, Williamson defends it off the back foot.
Shorter and quicker outside off, Williamson cuts it to backward point.
Full and outside off, Raval drives to the right of mid off and gives the strike back to the skipper.
Looped and on off, Williamson takes a step down and drives to mid on and is immediately off for a single. Easily into the crease at the non-striker's end as mid on has a shy at the stumps.
On length and angling in towards off stump, Raval defends it into the ground, this time off the front foot.
Good length outside off again and a beautiful drive through the covers this time. The boundary is quite long and the batsmen come back for three easily.

FOUR! What a classy shot! Good length and just outside off. Not much wrong with the ball but that's the class of the batsman. Williamson guides it beautifully in the gap towards the left of point for a boundary.
On a good length and just outside off, Kane defends to cover very watchfully.
Good length and on middle, Williamson is rock solid in defense.
Short and outside off, Williamson lets it go through to Sarfraz.
Short of a length and decent turn but way down the leg side, the left-hander wants to flick it away but misses the ball to be hit on his thigh guard.
Spins away and well down the leg side, Raval wants to poke it away in the gap but doesn't get willow on it.
Shorter and quicker on middle, Raval goes back in his crease and defends.
Goes slightly short this time, Raval just works it off his pads towards square leg.
Looped up on middle and spinning in, Raval plays it to mid-wicket.
Good drift on this ball after landing outside off, Raval tries to drive but gets the inside edge that goes onto the leg side.
On length and on the middle stump line, Williamson plays a wristy shot to short mid-wicket.
Surprise bouncer this time at the body, Raval jumps and manages to keep it down and plays it behind square on the leg side for a single.
On middle this time, Raval wants to drive it down the ground. The ball goes off the inner half of the bat, hits the pad and rolls onto the leg side. No run.
Well outside off on this occasion as the left-hander just shoulders his arms to it.
Fuller and outside off, Raval gets right behind the line of the delivery and defends it comfortably.
From around the wicket, slightly short of a length and on off. Raval goes back and defends it back to the bowler.
Not great bowling from Yasir, on the pads again, Williamson stays back and easily defends it toward short mid-wicket.
Shorter and quicker on middle, it is defended off the back foot by the batsman.
This ball is flighted and on middle, Raval makes room to drive it through the covers and picks up a single. New Zealand on level terms with Pakistan now.
Similar ball and similarly defended again.
Full and quick at the pads, Raval brings his bat ahead of his front leg and defends it.
Fuller and on leg stump, Raval plays it to short mid-wicket.
On a good length and just above off stump, the skipper defends presenting the full face of the bat.
Low bounce on this occasion and angling down the leg side, Williamson looks to help it on its way but the ball is way down leg for him to get bat on it.
Around the wicket this time, Raval takes a step forward and pushes into the gap through the covers and picks up three. New Zealand now trail only by a run.
On a length and off stump now, Raval is half ahead and defends it into the ground.
Slightly shorter and outside off this time. Comes in a bit after landing, Raval lets it go through watchfully.
On a good length and well outside off, Raval leaves it alone.
On the pads and slightly short this time, the leftie flicks it away to square leg for a single. Good over for New Zealand as 9 comes from it.
Full and outside off again, no spin yet. Raval comes ahead and defends again.
FOUR! Over the top this time, the ball is full and outside off again. Raval hits it over mid on for another boundary. Positive from intent from Raval this morning.
Quick one again on off stump, Raval defends on the front foot.
FOUR! The ball is full and on middle, Raval dances down the wicker and whips it through wide mid on, it beats the dive of that fielder and races to the fence.
Quicker and fuller on off, Raval comes ahead and defends it straight back to the bowler.
Slightly fuller and on off stump, Williamson defends as he is half-forward to this one.
Outside off and on a length again, Williamson shoulders arms again.
Well outside off this time, the skipper leaves it alone easily.
Back to just outside off and on a length, Williamson covers his off pole and then lets it go through.
Length ball on middle, Williamson presents the full face of the bat as he defends to mid on.
Starts off on a good length, Williamson stays inside the crease and defends with a straight bat.
Mohammad Abbas is into the attack.
Flatter and quicker on off stump, Raval stays back to this one and defends it.
Small appeal from the bowler but Raval was well ahead to that one. It was pitched outside off and he comes ahead to that one but misses it, the ball hits him on the front pad. Going down leg.
Full and flighted outside off this time, Raval prods ahead and dead bats it.
FOUR! Slightly shorter, Raval goes back and punches it straight down the ground to the long off fence. First boundary today.
Good length and starting on middle, spins away down leg and hits Raval on the pad as he comes ahead to defend.
Nice and flighted outside off, first run of the morning as Williamson comes forward and pushes it through cover for a single.
Yasir Shah to bowl from the other end.
Full and on off again, the batsman comes well forward and defends.
From around the wicket, nice and flighted on middle. Raval comes ahead and defends.
We are all set for the action to resume. Jeet Raval and Kane Williamson will resume their innings. Mohammad Hafeez will complete his over. He has two balls to go. Here we go...

The first hour of play will be crucial and New Zealand's skipper and best batsman, Kane Williamson will have to shoulder the responsibility of guiding the Black Caps through this phase of play. The pitch is certainly a tough one to play on but not unplayable. Pakistan, on the other hand will be looking to knock off the mainstay and bowl out the visitors cheaply as batting fourth on this pitch will be really tricky and they'd like their target to be as low as possible. Join us for live action in a bit!

Welcome to Day 3 of the first Test between Pakistan and New Zealand. We have had riveting action over the past two days and the match is pretty evenly poised right now. New Zealand after a dismal Day 1 have done really well to recover and pull this game back on Day 2 and generate interest. Looking forward to today's play, one of the factors could be how the weather behaves. There is forecast for showers over the day but we hope it stays away as the Test enters the 'moving day' and we will get a fair idea as to who will be ahead by the end of today.
... Day 3, Session 1 ...

The surface was expected to prefer the batsmen, but it has proved quite even and provided something to all. Day 3 is poised quite well and it could make for good viewing for the neutrals. That is, of course, if it doesn't rain as there's some forecast for it. For now, the action will begin on time at 1000 local (0600 GMT). Do join in for all the action. Take care!

A good day for the Black Caps. They took 8 Pakistan wickets since the day started, restricting the lead to just 74 runs. Trent Boult was the leader of the pack as he ran riot with a 4-wicket haul, with the rest chipping in with handy contributions of their own. If not for Babar Azam and his solid fifty, Pakistan's lead would have been slimmer. In response, New Zealand lost Latham early as Hasan Ali removed him but Kane Williamson and Jeet Raval have looked as assured as anyone after that with their stand currently unbeaten on 56. Their team trails by just 18 runs.
So, the umpires take another reading and decide it isn't good enough now to continue. Play has been called off due to bad light. That's STUMPS ON DAY 2!
Around the wicket now, floated on off, blocked from the front foot.
Flat and short on leg, Kane works it off his pads and sends it to deep mid-wicket for one run.
Quite slow through the air, fuller around off, Williamson is well forward in defense.
Minimal spin around off, kept out off the back foot.
The umpire takes out his light meter and checks. The reading shows it's fine enough to continue. The floodlights are on. Also, Mohammad Hafeez into the attack now.
The ball is down the leg side but the batsman still goes after it. Misses it in the end.
The leg break spinning in a long way from outside off, Jeet goes back and works it down on the leg side.
Extremely full outside off, pushed square towards point.
Flat and short on off, forced from the back foot to sweeper cover for a single.
Leg spinner outside off, on a driving length, Williamson comes forward to defend but gets beaten.
Good running between the wickets. Raval wrists this towards Bilal at mid on and both batsmen take off. There is a shy at the non-striker's end but it misses. Had he hit, would have been close.
Spinning down leg, Williamson looks to flick but misses.
Full delivery outside off, driven square on the off side for a single.

FOUR! Floated on middle and off, Raval gets forward and across before bringing out the lap shot. Connects well, uses the pace and finds the fine leg fence. Beats the chasing fielder. Good shot. The 50 comes up for New Zealand, they trail by 22 runs.
Full and slow on off, blocked with the full face.
Landed outside off on a driving length, Jeet shoulders arms to it.
Flatter and quicker angling in on leg, Raval gets low and paddles it fine down the leg side. He'll get a brace for it.
Tad quicker through the air on off, punched back in the bowler's direction to end the over.
Turning away from around off, on a shorter length, punched away square towards point.
Flights it right up there, on middle and leg, a front foot defensive shot is presented in response.
Short and flat, on off, whipped from the back foot to deep mid-wicket for a couple.
Quicker and fuller outside off, Kane defends.
Full, loopy and on the stumps, drilled towards mid on for no run.
Moves across his sticks as the ball spins into him and clips it to the man at square leg for one.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads.
Kane goes on the back foot and works it away on the leg side.
Quite full outside off from around the wicket, it's driven through the gap in the covers for one more.
Touch short around off, Kane works it square on the leg side and changes ends.
Full and straight, on the stumps, turned away in front of square leg.
Quick, flat and short outside off, punched off the back foot to covers.
Sharp spin into the batsman, catches him on the thigh pad as he looks to play off the back foot.
Sarfraz bringing another close-in fielder. A silly point in place now, along with the slip and short leg already positioned.
Floated outside off, and coming in, Raval prods forward to defend but is caught on the front pad. Impact well outside off.
Watches the ball carefully, waits for it to turn into him and then defends off the back foot.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Serves it on a driving length, coming in from outside off, the southpaw comes forward and blocks.
Goes on the back foot this time and works it to short leg once more.
Williamson comes forward, plays with the spin as he turns it to short leg.
Looped up, outside off, pushed through covers off the front foot for one.
Outside off, turning away, left alone.
The short of length delivery has been cut away through square on the off side. The batsmen have picked up a couple of runs.
Going away on the stumps, worked away on the leg side.
Bilal Asif is on to bowl.

That's missed everything completely! Great catch from umpire Bruce Oxenford. Yasir tosses it up around off, Raval goes down to sweep but misses and the ball goes through his legs. It races away behind as the batsmen take three. Everybody thought it was a leg bye, except for umpire Oxenford.
Waits for the ball to come to him, hangs back and blocks it well.
A lot of revs on this, outside off, Raval presses forward to get close to the pitch and gets an inside edge back onto his pads.
Short and flat, spinning away from outside off, cut to sweeper cover for a single.
Quite full on off, drilled out on the off side.
Full and straight, Kane Williamson is well forward in defense.
FOUR! Welcome runs for Raval and New Zealand. Full and swinging back in, it's flicked through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Full delivery just outside off, defensively pushed towards the cover fielder.
Good length ball on the fifth stump line, arms are shouldered to let it through.
On a length on off, defended in front of cover from within the crease.
Brave leave. Length delivery just around off, shapes in and Raval leaves. Probably was missing off all along, but maybe even Raval didn't think it'd be this close to the off stump.
Full length delivery shaping in on off, Jeet drives towards mid off.

Drinks are on the field. Pakistan got the early wicket of Latham thanks to a beauty from Hasan Ali, but haven't been able to take advantage of that. Williamson and Raval have done well to get their eye in and both look good. If this pair can see the day off, the visitors will be a happy bunch.
Quick, straight and short on the stumps, punched straight back to the bowler.
Short and wide, Kane cuts but can't beat the man at point.
Leans ahead to the full ball and eases it to mid off.
Positions himself behind the line and blocks it out.
Tossed up well outside off, going away, forces Williamson to play away from the body and the edge is drawn. Luckily for the Kiwi captain, it goes wide of first slip to third man. Two to the total.
Bit quicker through the air on middle and leg, pushed back down the track off the back foot.
Good length ball on off, Raval nicely gets behind the line and blocks it with a straight bat.

Beaten on the drive this time! Abbas serves it on a fuller length outside off and gets it to shape away, Raval is tempted into the drive and is beaten. Abbas is getting closer and closer to taking his first wicket.

Beauty to beat the bat! Abbas is unreal to southpaws from 'round the wicket angle. His line just around off coupled with a wee bit of away movement always catches the batsman in trouble. This time Jeet is lucky not to edge it.
Pitches it on a length around off, Raval drives it towards extra cover where Bilal Asif dives and parries it to mid off. Good effort!
Once again Raval prods forward to defend but this time it takes the inside edge and deflects off his pads to covers.
Angles in a length ball on off, from 'round the wicket, Raval defends it off his front foot.
Picks up the length early as it's flat and short outside off, punched through covers for a couple of runs.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. They have run through for a single.
Stays right behind the line and defends well.
Coming in once more, Jeet is deep inside the crease as he looks to turn it in front of short leg. Is rapped on the pads instead.
Outside off, with some width on offer, played through point for a brace.

The inside edge has saved him there. Yasir flights it up outside off, it spins back in off the rough as Raval presses forward to defend. The ball strikes his back pad, but not before taking the inside edge.
Yasir Shah returns.
Touch fuller in length, it's blocked comfortably to end the over.
Too straight in line, wristed in front of square leg.

Not out! Williamson survives. Poor review from all involved. Abbas angles it in on middle and leg, it keeps going down and catches Kane on the pads. A big appeal goes up, but the umpire shakes his head. Abbas speaks with his skipper and then it's taken upstairs. Replays show the ball to be missing the leg stump. Clearly. Review lost.
Review taken. It's taken by Pakistan for an lbw decision against Kane Williamson. Looks to be going down leg to the naked eye.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Length delivery aiming the top of off stump, stays inside the crease and blocks it back down the track.
Tad straight in line, attacks the stumps, Kane blocks it down in front of mid-wicket.
Mohammad Abbas is back on.
Floats it right up there, Jeet is well forward in defense.
Uses the depth of the crease again, Raval has enough time to go back and turn it on the leg side.
Goes deep inside the crease, adjusts and works it to backward square leg.
Goes with the spin and turns it to square leg.
Short and wide outside off, slapped the punch to sweeper cover for a single.
A lot of air on off stump, driven to mid off.
Haris Sohail to roll his arm over.

Shout for a leg before, turned down. Maybe an inside edge there. Looped up leg break around off, turns in sharply and catches Jeet Raval on the pads as he prods ahead to defend. Seems some bat is involved.
Spinning away from the batsman, it's cut through to sweeper cover for a run.
FOUR! But that was a close one. Quicker one from Yasir, Williamson backs away to cut and almost gets bowled. Luckily, he played it well enough to cut it past short third man for a boundary.
Well left. Kane watches the ball as it turns away from him, covers the line and lets it be.
Turning in from a shorter length this time, goes back and punches it through the covers. One run collected.
Tossed up leg break from around the wicket, spinning in, Raval presses forward and defends.
Some more chin music for the New Zealand captain. He just ducks under it and lets it pass.
Short and wide outside off, no way Williamson will play at that.
Back of a length delivery, close to off, kept out safely from within the crease.
Outside off, left alone for the keeper to collect.
Full in length, attacking the stumps, another defensive shot from Williamson.
Full ball outside off, blocked off the front foot.
Loopy, slow and full outside off, invites Williamson forward and he pushes it through covers to keep strike.
Quicker and shorter, flicked off the back foot to deep mid-wicket for a run.
Goes with the spin and turns it on the leg side with soft hands.
Tossed up in line of the stumps, pushed back down the track.
Looped up leg break, driven from the front foot through the covers for one.
The flipper on off stump, Kane backs away and forces the punch to point.
Yasir Shah is into the attack now.
Seaming into the left-hander from a fullish length, blocked off the front foot to end the over.
In the channel outside off, arms are shouldered confidently.
Keeps it on the fuller side, but brings it back in just outside off, Raval takes a step forward and meets it with the full face.
Full ball outside the line of off stump, driven to the mid off fielder.
Coming in again but the line is a touch straight, Jeet whips this behind square leg and comes back for the second.
From around the wicket and wide of the crease, swinging back in, Raval is rock solid in defense. Plays it down on the leg side.
Keeps it close to off, it's defensively punched square to point.
Targets the off stump with a length delivery, blocked with a straight blade in response.
Wide outside off, reaches out to it and slaps it to the man at cover-point.
Beaten! After bringing two back in, Abbas makes this one go away. On a back of a length, Williamson pushes inside the line and misses.
Attacks the stumps, doesn't give Williamson much room with this length ball. The batter can only stay behind the line and block.
Cutting back in from a good length, on middle and leg, worked down in front of mid-wicket.
Good carry on that. Hasan pitches it in the channel outside off, the southpaw lets it be as Sarfraz collects it at chest height.
Almost dragged it back on! Back of a length just outside off, coming back in, Raval with no foot movement gets an inside edge which thuds onto his pads.
Short of a good length outside off, the Kiwi skipper punches it through the gap in the covers. Three good runs taken.
FOUR! Too straight once again from Hasan Ali and he pays the price. Can't bowl it to him there. Williamson flicks it away sweetly through the vacant square leg region and finds the fence.
Too straight in line, allows Raval to work this down towards fine leg for a single.
Coming back in from outside off, full in length, Jeet blocks with a defensive blade in response.
Over the wicket, length delivery which keeps a bit low. Williamson does well to bring his bat down and force it away on the off side.
Fraction straight in line, flicked towards mid-wicket where Bilal Asif makes a diving stop to his left. The batsmen cross over.
Offers no shot this time. Sees the ball landing outside off on a length, he covers the line and lets it through.
Lovely full length, shaping back around off, Raval with the full face of the bat blocks it in front of cover.
Bit fuller around off, Jeet prods forward and pushes it with hard hands to cover.
From around the wicket to Raval, a good length ball is seaming back in on off. The left-hander stands his ground and blocks it down on the off side.
Well left. Excellent over from Hasan Ali comes to an end. He hurls it in the off stump channel, Kane covers the line and makes a watchful leave.
Outside the line of off stump, Williamson confidently offers a firm punch which finds the cover fielder.
Length delivery outside off, punched off the back foot to short cover.
Back to around the wicket to the left-hander, it's angled in on a back of a length, Raval too gets off the mark as he works it down in front of square leg for one.
Over the wicket now to Kane. Fuller length ball on off, it's flicked behind square on the leg side for a single. Williamson is off the mark immediately.
Kane Williamson is in at no.3.

OUT! Bowled first ball! What a beginning from Hasan Ali. Nothing Tom Latham could have done about that, really. Incredible delivery first up. Hasan Ali comes from around the wicket and bowls it around off, it shapes back in as Latham hangs his bat down the wrong line. The off stump goes for the toss and that's the first breakthrough for the home side.
Hasan Ali to bowl from the other end.
Good length delivery outside the line of off stump, left alone to end the over.
That's a brave leave from Jeet Raval. Abbas pitches it close to off on a length and as Raval lets it go, it nips back in. Whiskers past the off stick. Super close, that.
Just ahead of a length, on the fourth stump line, Raval plants his front foot forward and shoulders arms.
Third leave in a row. Expect more of this with Abbas bowling. He keeps probing in that off stump channel, left alone.
Good shape on that. Mohammad Abbas hurls it on a length once more, quite close to off, Raval once again leaves it alone.
Angling across on a good length, Raval watchfully lets it be.
